author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Create a usable touchscreen control layout
summary: Design touch controls around reach, visibility, simultaneous actions, pressure needs, and repeatable gameplay tests instead of shrinking a full DualShock 2 onto the display.
heroAlt: EmuCoreX gameplay with translucent touchscreen sticks and PlayStation-style buttons

blocks.text: Design for the actions a game combines

A readable screenshot is not automatically a playable touch layout. PS2 games may require moving a stick while holding a shoulder button, tapping a face button and adjusting the camera. The layout must reserve comfortable thumb arcs, avoid system-gesture edges and leave critical UI visible. Different genres deserve different profiles rather than one crowded universal overlay.
Duplicate a working preset before editing. Keep an untouched fallback so a misplaced invisible control cannot lock you out of gameplay.

List the game's frequent, held and rare actions. Note whether it uses both sticks, analog button pressure, rapid tapping or diagonal D-pad input. Decide landscape orientation and whether Android navigation is gesture or three-button, because safe edges differ.

items: A duplicate of the default touch profile.
One training area or early save with no penalty.
Screen orientation and system navigation mode fixed.
A list of simultaneous input combinations.
Touch visualization or input feedback enabled when available.

blocks.text: Build the layout from high-frequency actions

items: 1. Place movement and camera sticks under natural thumb resting points, leaving travel room around each centre.
2. Position primary face and shoulder actions so the most common two-button combination can be held without crossing fingers.
3. Move Start, Select and rare actions away from combat zones and reduce their opacity only after their hit areas are proven.
4. Assign pressure controls only where the game reads pressure; provide a deliberate alternate or slider when partial pressure matters.
5. Save under a game-specific name, restart the title and test walking, diagonals, camera, held actions and a three-touch combination.

blocks.text: Play for at least ten minutes without looking at your thumbs. Controls should respond at their visible centres and not trigger neighboring buttons. Test near Android gesture edges and on any display cutout side. A control may be visually subtle only if its hitbox remains discoverable and does not cover important HUD information.

items: Both sticks reach full cardinal and diagonal range.
Common held-plus-tap combinations register reliably.
No system gesture steals an essential input.
Buttons match their visible hit areas.
The fallback preset still loads.

blocks.text: If a control disappears or overlaps badly, load the untouched preset and duplicate it again. Revert the last group of changes rather than dragging every element at once. Export or back up the accepted profile before trying a different orientation or screen size.

items: Load the default/fallback profile.
Restore opacity and scale for missing controls.
Reset only the current game's touch assignment.
Recreate the layout separately for another aspect ratio.
Button appears responsive alone but fails while moving: multitouch combination was not tested.
Edge control opens Android navigation: gesture exclusion was ignored.
Stick cannot reach full range: visual scale and analog radius disagree.
One profile feels wrong on tablet: physical reach changed with screen size.

blocks.text: Treat a touch profile like a controller mapping with ergonomics. Name it by game, orientation and device class, keep a revision that passed the full combination test, and make later changes in small groups. The result should prioritize reliable actions over decorative symmetry.
